text:
sanam: Heads up — we're seeing gRPC streaming stalls from model-serving pods in the GPU pool (us-west-2). Pod->pod streams across nodes will hang for ~3-10s then recover. Root logs show repeated: 
```
rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = transport is closing
stream send failed: write tcp 10.42.3.12:52344->10.42.7.21:50051: write: connection timed out
# also lots of: gRPC stream no bytes for 5000ms
```

chris_k: Is it only cross-node? same-node unaffected? Any recent infra changes (kernel, NIC drivers, CNI)?

sanam: Same-node fine. Cross-node only. We just rolled a small set of new baremetal hosts with a different NIC driver + kernel. CNI is Cilium with vxlan overlay for this pool. Quick ip link from two nodes:
```
# node-a (older hosts)
2: eth0: mtu 1500 qdisc fq_codel state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    link/ether aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:01
4: vxlan0: mtu 1450 qdisc pfifo_fast state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
# node-b (new host)
2: eth0: mtu 1450 qdisc fq_codel state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
4: vxlan0: mtu 1450 qdisc pfifo_fast state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
```

sanam: note: new host eth0 came up 1450 because cloud-init/netplan applied mtu for our provider overlay. So some hosts have eth0@1500 while others 1450.

alex.s: MTU mismatch across nodes + VXLAN encapsulation = fragmentation risk. Also check if GSO/GRO/TSO offloads are interacting badly with vxlan. When offloads are on, the kernel may hand down giant skbs that get split/fragged by the overlay and the reassembly can stall streams. Run ethtool -k on the NICs and compare.

irina: Saw similar before. tcpdump on host shows lots of IP fragments and reassembly warnings in dmesg: 
```
Apr 12 11:23:02 node-b kernel: nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packets
Apr 12 11:23:02 node-b kernel: IPv4: bad checksum. Dropping frame
Apr 12 11:23:02 node-b kernel: ip_frag: cache flushed, reassembly fragmented packet timed out
```
Also captured a short dump: many fragments with frag offsets. gRPC's streaming uses long lived connections and small windows; fragmentation + reordering can cause the underlying TCP segments to stall until reassembly floods.

chris_k: Can you paste ethtool -k for both eth0s and vxlan? Also try disabling GRO/TSO as a quick test on one node pair: `sudo ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off` (and same for the veth pair for pods). If that fixes, we know offload+encap/mtu interaction is the culprit.

sanam: Ran quick tests. iperf3 between pods across nodes before/after disables: 
```
# before
[ ID] Interval           Transfer     Bandwidth       Retr
[  5]   0.00-10.00  sec   850 MBytes  712 Mbits/sec  2120             (lots of retransmits)
# after (disabled offloads)
[  5]   0.00-10.00  sec   1.1 GBytes  946 Mbits/sec   12
```
Also ran `ping -M do -s` to test PMTUD behavior: path breaks around 1380 payload (VXLAN overhead), and do=don't fragment packets are being dropped on some hops.

alex.s: That matches. Two paths: either standardize MTU across hosts to a safe value (e.g., host mtu 1500 with tunnel mtu adjusted) or enable jumbo consistently (9000) everywhere. For immediate mitigation: set Cilium tunnelMTU to min(host MTU) - overhead (e.g., 1400) and rollout; that avoids fragmentation. And turn off LSO/GSO on hosts where kernel/NIC combo is buggy.

irina: For longer term, schedule a rolling standardization of host MTU in the GPU pool. Also file a bug with NIC vendor driver if some hosts negotiate 1450 unexpectedly. I'll open an infra ticket to coordinate.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1304 - mtumismatch-gso-vxlan-impacting-grpc (priority: P2) <https://redwood.internal/incident/INC-2026-1304>

sanam: Plan: 1) apply Cilium configmap change (tunnelMTU: 1400) on the GPU Cilium DaemonSet and restart cilium pods; 2) disable GRO/TSO on the 3 new hosts as emergency workaround; 3) monitor gRPC error rate and latencies for 2 hours; 4) schedule host-MTU standardization next week + vendor driver followup. Will update here after the rollout. :thumbsup:

chris_k: If you need a quick script to flip offloads and check mtu, ping me. We should also add an e2e test in our chaos harness to detect mtu mismatches during upgrades.

sanam: Update — after applying tunnelMTU=1400 and disabling offloads on the three new hosts, gRPC stall incidents dropped to zero in the next 30m window. Leaving monitoring in place and will proceed with the full remediation plan tomorrow. :thumbsup:
